evidence: Downloaded the Transportstyrelsen COLREG.2 compilation (https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/globalassets/global/sjofart/dokument/sjotrafik_dok/imo_colreg.2_cirkular.pdf?id=58526). COLREG.2/Circ.44 (May 1998, MSC 69) lists '.1 At One Fathom Bank (amended scheme) and the precautionary area Off Port Klang' and para 2 says implementation is at 0000 UTC on 1 December 1998. Annex 1 gives the lane limits from (9) 03°02'.70N to (13) 02°41'.20N, and the precautionary area runs south to 02°39'.40N, so the stated span is correct. The quoted passage in the record is actually para 1.4/2 wording for Malacca to Iyu Kecil, but it paraphrases the same circular and item .1 is present. In PC 65/1998 (https://www.mpa.gov.sg/api/media/78c165e3-67e4-4da3-9496-c196739374d2/-pc98-65.pdf), MSC.73(69) Annex 1 para 2.1 has the verbatim text 'The area includes the routeing system in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore', para 3.4 has 'Sector 1 to Sector 5 - Klang VTS', and Appendix 3 has Sector 1 ch 66 and Sector 2 ch 88 (Klang VTS). The live MPA Operational Areas page shows the same table. Sector logic: I rendered SPI 2026 p.119 (https://file.go.gov.sg/spi2026apr17.pdf, Appendix 1) and measured it against the graticule. The Sector 1/2 boundary is the thin dashed line from the western reporting point to Port Klang at about 02°52'N, and the TSS lanes cross it. The Sector 2/3 boundary crosses the routeing system SE of the Off Port Klang precautionary area, so the scheme lies in Sectors 1 and 2 as claimed. STRAITREP is an IMO-adopted SOLAS mandatory SRS and is not routine VTS reporting.

COLREG.2/Circ.44 in the Transportstyrelsen compilation lists '.4 Malacca to Iyu Kecil (new scheme) and the precautionary area Off Sultan Shoal Lighthouse', implemented 1 Dec 1998, and I confirmed the quoted passage. Annex 4 coordinates run from (53) 02°05'.40N 102°04'.60E and DW (80) 02°00'N 101°59'.80E to (70) 01°14'.30N 103°29'.70E and (76) 01°09'.20N 103°26'.80E. COLREG.2/Circ.54 (28 May 2004, same compilation) para 1.5 lists 'In the Singapore Strait' (amended scheme), and para 2 gives implementation at 0000 UTC on 1 January 2005 for annex 5. The claim is correct, but the cited source entry for Circ.54 gives the wrong title and passage (Ra's al Kuh / Ra's al Khafji, 1 Dec 2004). Sector check against the MSC.73(69) text in PC 65/1998 and the SPI 2026 chartlets pp.119-120: the Tg Piai (01°15'.50N 103°30'.75E) to Karimun Kecil (01°09'.20N 103°24'.35E) line interpolates to 103°29'.53E at 01°14'.30N. Point 70 is therefore about 0.2' east of the line and point 76 about 2.4' east, so both are marginally in Sector 7, as the record says. The Off Sultan Shoal precautionary area (points 81-84, 103°26'.76E to 103°36'.24E) lies in Sector 7. On Appendix 1 the thin Sector 3/4 boundary line (P. Rupat to Malacca) crosses at the SE edge of the Off Malacca/Dumai precautionary area, where the scheme's DW route begins, so the NW tip may just touch Sector 3. Sector 3 is also Klang VTS (ch 84), so the VTS list is unaffected. The MPA 'Vessels Arriving in Singapore' page confirms VTIS West ch 73 = Sector 7, 'between the line joining Tg Piai and Pulau Karimun Kecil and Long. 103°44.5'E'.
recommended_change: Correct the Circ.54 cited_source entry: title 'COLREG.2/Circ.54 New and amended traffic separation schemes (28 May 2004)', locator 'para 1.5 and para 2, annex 5', passage: 'the amendment to the existing traffic separation scheme "In the Singapore Strait" (annex 5) will be implemented at 0000 hours UTC on 1 January 2005'. Optionally add 'NW tip at the Sector 3/4 boundary (Sector 3 also Klang VTS, ch 84)'.

evidence: COLREG.2/Circ.44 para 1.8 lists 'At Horsburgh Lighthouse Area (amended scheme)', implemented 1 Dec 1998, and Annex 8 is in the Transportstyrelsen compilation. SPI 2025 (https://file.go.gov.sg/spi2025feb01.pdf) p.15 and SPI 2026 p.15 give the WGS 84 coordinates 104°14.89'E to (150) 01°23.40'N 104°27.84'E with 'Source: COLREG.2/Circ.44 dated 26 May 1998 with amendments from COLREG.2/Circ.54'. The Circ.44 original uses Revised Kertau datum, so its (150) 104°27'.95E differs slightly, which is immaterial. MSC.73(69) (IMO PDF https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MSCResolutions/MSC.73(69).pdf, Annex 10/Annex 1 para 2.1) limits STRAITREP to 100°40'E to 104°23'E and lists Horsburgh Lt (01°19'.81N 104°24'.44E) as a reference point in para 3.3.3, and I confirmed the quote. The MPA Vessels Arriving page says VTIS East ch 10 covers 'Sector 9 ... between Long. 104°02.1'E and 104°23.0'E', and the SPI Appendix 2 chartlet shows the Long 104°22.9'E limit line with the TSS extending east of it. The partial-coverage wording for both VTS and STRAITREP is accurate. I found no source for the portion east of 104°23'E, which the record does not claim.

COLREG.2/Circ.74 (BIMCO copy https://bimco.org/media/gusfhkrc/colreg2circ74-new-traffic-separation-schemes-secretariat.pdf) is dated 14 June 2019 and records MSC 101 adoption of '.1 In the Sunda Strait; and .2 In the Lombok Strait', with 'should be implemented on 1 July 2020'. The annex includes an Inshore Traffic Zone, and I confirmed the quote. The DGST news release (https://hubla.dephub.go.id/home/post/read/7657/...) contains the verbatim text 'Sistem Pelaporan dan Informasi Navigasi di Selat Sunda dan Selat Lombok bersifat wajib, yaitu bagi semua kapal berbendera Indonesia yang melintas' and 'Bagi TSS Selat Sunda melalui Radio VHF pada channel 22 atau 68 dengan nama panggil Merak VTS', and names the systems 'SUNDAREP dan LOMBOKREP'. The same release says foreign ships are only 'sangat dianjurkan untuk berpartisipasi' (strongly recommended to participate). The KM references read 'KM 129 Tahun 2020 tentang Penetapan Sistem Rute di Selat Lombok' and 'KM 130 Tahun 2020 tentang Penetapan Sistem Rute di Selat Lombok dan Selat Sunda' (sic), so assigning KM 130 to Sunda is plausible but the source is garbled. Hubla post 5132 confirms MSC 101 adoption but does not mention VTS or reporting. SUNDAREP is a named system set by ministerial decree, so it is a separate scheme and not routine VTS reporting. It is mandatory only for Indonesian-flag ships. One extra search found no IMO adoption of SUNDAREP/LOMBOKREP.
recommended_change: Reporting note: append 'Foreign ships: participation strongly recommended (voluntary) per DGST; not IMO-adopted.' Consider flagging as 'Confirmed present (national, flag-limited)'. Cite KM 130/2020 with the caveat that the DGST release's title wording is garbled.

evidence: COLREG.2/Circ.74 (BIMCO copy) para 1.2 is 'In the Lombok Strait' and the annex heading is 'IN THE LOMBOK STRAIT' with an Inshore Traffic Zone. The record's locator wrongly points to the Sunda annex. The DGST release (hubla post 7657) contains the verbatim text '...TSS Selat Lombok melalui Radio VHF pada channel 16 atau 68 dengan nama panggil Benoa VTS', which supports the VTS claim. It also says the reporting system is mandatory for all Indonesian-flag ships and only strongly recommended for foreign ships entering the TSS.
recommended_change: Change the Circ.74 locator to 'Paras 1 and 2; Annex "In the Lombok Strait"'. Append to the reporting note: 'Foreign ships: participation strongly recommended (voluntary); not IMO-adopted.'

evidence: The Paper article (https://m.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_30326627, 6 Mar 2025) is published by the official '广东海事' (Guangdong MSA) account, not Guangzhou MSA as the record says. It confirms the TSS composition (第一、第二通航分道，第一、第二分隔带，沿岸通航带，以及第一、第二警戒区) and the text '如遇紧急情况可在VHF08\09频道上向广州交管中心请求协助'. That means the VTS can be called for help in an emergency; it does not state VTS coverage. The radar screenshot is labelled as accident-investigation material, not a VTS coverage statement. The Chinanews report (https://www.chinanews.com.cn/dwq/2026/04-08/10600653.shtml, secondary, photos credited to Guangzhou MSA) says the Guangzhou VTS Centre's '担杆' station '8日正式投入试运行' and '将对担杆水道分道通航制...开展常态化VTS管控'. This implies the TSS was not under routine VTS control before April 2026, and on 8 April 2026 it entered only trial operation. No primary MSA notice defining the VTS area over the TSS was found. One search in Chinese returned only Hong Kong Marine Department notices, which are not relevant. WebFetch returned 503 for the Guangdong MSA 解读 page, but curl retrieved it. It confirms '珠江口VTS区域报告线共21条' and the principle '报进不报出，报离不报靠', and gives the Pearl River Estuary special supervision area as 东至114°30′08.8″E, 南至21°48′00.0″N. These are VTS reporting lines (routine VTS reporting), not a separate SRS, so reporting stays 'Unresolved' and cannot be 'Confirmed absent'.
recommended_change: VTS: downgrade from 'Confirmed present' to 'Unresolved (probable; Guangzhou VTS Centre Dangan station in trial operation from 8 Apr 2026 per Chinanews, secondary)' until a Guangzhou or Guangdong MSA notice defines VTS coverage. Correct the S13 publisher to Guangdong MSA (广东海事) and describe VHF 08/09 as emergency assistance only.

evidence: MSC.389(94) (IMO PDF https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MSCResolutions/MSC%20389%2094.pdf) is adopted under SOLAS V/11 and enters into force at 0000 UTC on 1 June 2015. It contains the verbatim text 'The waters covered by the Ship Reporting System is the water area with the VTS Centre (geographical position is 37°23'.65N, 122°42'.12E) as the centre and 24 miles as the radius', names the authority as Weihai MSA with call sign 'Chengshan Jiao VTS Centre' (radar, 24-hour watch), and refers to ships 'at anchor in the TSSs'. The researcher missed that the adoption instruments are in the same Transportstyrelsen compilation already cited for other records. COLREG.2/Circ.48 (1 June 2000, MSC 72) para 1.7 'In the waters Off the Chengsan Jian Promontory (new scheme)', implemented 0000 UTC 1 December 2000, is at compilation p.189 annex 7. COLREG.2/Circ.66 (21 November 2014, MSC 94) para 1.2 'In the waters off the Chengshan Jiao Promontory' (amended), implemented 0000 UTC 1 June 2015, with the note 'See mandatory ship reporting system Off the Chengshan Jiao Promontory', is at p.427 onwards. I checked the Circ.66 coordinates against the 24 nm radius. Most points lie inside (e.g. (16) 37°44'.00N 122°51'.56E about 22 nm; (28) 37°11'.60N 123°04'.14E about 21 nm). The easternmost outer-TSS point (23) 37°34'.76N 123°11'.30E is about 25.7 nm out, just beyond the radius. Coverage is therefore of nearly all of the scheme, which meets the rule.
recommended_change: Identity note: replace 'TSS adoption instrument and dates not retrieved' with 'Adopted MSC 72, COLREG.2/Circ.48 (1 June 2000), implemented 1 Dec 2000; amended MSC 94, COLREG.2/Circ.66 (21 Nov 2014), implemented 1 June 2015 (Transportstyrelsen COLREG.2 compilation).' VTS/reporting note: add 'the eastern end of the outer TSS lies marginally beyond the 24 nm SRS/VTS radius'.

evidence: The Meganorm copy of Government Directive 1226-r of 2 Sept 2006 (https://meganorm.ru/Data2/1/4293849/4293849842.htm) contains 'Схема разделения движения № 3. Между мысами Поворотный и Островной'. Part I runs from 133°17,50'E, Part II from 42°38,30'N 133°26,50'E to 42°42,80'N 133°46,80'E, and Part III to 133°42,00'E. It also contains 'Плавание иностранных судов по полосе движения, расположенной к северо-западу от зоны разделения части II, запрещается'. Caveats: Meganorm is an unofficial mirror of an official act. I did not verify that the Directive is still current or that the scheme corresponds to an IMO-listed 'Off Ostrovnoi Point' TSS. A search of the COLREG.2 compilation found only 'In the approaches to the Gulf of Nakhodka' (Circ.38, 1992), not Ostrovnoi. The record already says 'IMO adoption not verified'. On RG.ru (https://rg.ru/documents/2011/07/05/naxodka-site-dok.html), Order 169 of 2011 establishes the RSUDS of Peter the Great Gulf and says approach sector 1Б is bounded south by the territorial sea, west by 132°28,00' and east by 133°43,00', with communication on VHF ch 9. Parts I and III and most of Part II fall inside those meridians, so the partial-coverage claim is accurate. Currency risk: the order is dated 2011 (as amended to 2017), and one search found no newer Nakhodka regulations; many Russian ports have had their Обязательные постановления replaced since 2021. Reporting 'Unresolved' is appropriate.
recommended_change: Add the caveat 'Order 169/2011 currency not confirmed (latest edition seen 15.12.2017); verify against current Обязательные постановления for Nakhodka/Vostochny'. Identity note: add 'Directive text from an unofficial mirror (meganorm); official publication not fetched.'

evidence: The AMSA offshore page (https://www.amsa.gov.au/safety-navigation/navigating-coastal-waters/offshore-oil-and-gas-exploration) lists 'Cape Leeuwin Traffic Separation Scheme (TSS)' under South-West and Southern Australia and states that activities are not permitted within 'any charted International Maritime Organization-adopted Traffic Separation Scheme'. The IMO primary the researcher said was missing is in the same Transportstyrelsen COLREG.2 compilation. COLREG.2/Circ.67 (20 May 2016, MSC 96) para 1.1 lists 'Off Southwest Australia (new scheme)', implemented at 0000 UTC on 1 December 2016. Annex 1 describes 'I Off Cape Leeuwin' (34°00'S to 34°37'S, 114°33'E to 114°57'E) and 'II Off Chatham Island' (35°23'S to 35°35'S, 116°20'E to 116°40'E). VTS: the AMSA 'VTS areas in Australia' page (https://amsa.gov.au/safety-navigation/navigating-coastal-waters/vts-areas-australia) lists every entity authorised to provide VTS in Australia (Marine Order 64). The only Western Australian entries are Fremantle Ports (Fremantle) and Pilbara Ports; there is nothing for Bunbury, Busselton, Albany or the south-west coast. This authoritative, exhaustive list supports 'Confirmed absent' for both schemes, by inference from the complete list of authorised providers rather than from an explicit sentence. MASTREP page: 'mandatory for certain vessels' under the Navigation Act 2012 and MO 63. For foreign vessels it applies only 'from the arrival at its first port in Australia until its departure from its final port', and it uses automatic AIS position reports. International through-traffic past Cape Leeuwin on its first arrival or after its final departure is therefore outside MASTREP.
recommended_change: Identity: cite COLREG.2/Circ.67 (20 May 2016), annex 1, implemented 1 Dec 2016, and drop 'not confirmed from a primary source'. VTS: change to 'Confirmed absent' citing the AMSA VTS areas page (no authorised VTS provider covers SW Australian coastal waters; Fremantle VTS is port-limited), noting it rests on the exhaustive authorised-provider list. Reporting: add 'foreign ships only between first arrival and final departure in Australia; AIS-based automatic reporting'.

evidence: Marad PDF (https://marad.gov.ua/storage/app/sites/1/international-activities/Propozicii_sistemi_rozpodilu_ryhu_en.pdf) contains the verbatim text 'combine 2 previously adopted by the IMO systems into one system' and refers to the TSS 'adopted by the IMO on 22.04.1981 (COLREG.2/Circ.14)' and to 'The VTS of the State Enterprise Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority (SE USPA) Pilotage Branch - Delta Pilot'. The Transportstyrelsen compilation p.30 (poor OCR) lists '.2 between the ports of Odessa and Ilichevsk; .3 in the approaches to the ports of Odessa and Ilichevsk'. The HKSOA summary (https://hksoa.org/member_circulars/colreg-2-circ-78-new-separation-schemes-and-associated-measures/) states that the Circ.78 amended schemes 'Approaches to the Chornomorsk, Odesa and Pivdennyi ports ... replace the existing traffic separation schemes Between the ports of Odessa and Ilichevsk and In the approaches to the ports of Odessa and Ilichevsk', implemented 0000 UTC 1 June 2023. One search for the IMO circular itself found no primary copy. The USPA notice of 29.07.2022 names 'pilot-operator of VTCP Odesa' (Delta-Lotsman) and caravan VHF channels, but does not define a VTS area or a reporting scheme, so 'Unresolved' for VTS and reporting is correctly cautious.
recommended_change: Because the scheme is superseded, set VTS and reporting to 'Not applicable (superseded; see successor "Approaches to the Chornomorsk, Odesa and Pivdennyi ports")' or carry the open questions to the successor record. Keep the note that the Circ.78 replacement rests on a secondary summary.
